builder_plan.scenario: Profiling shows attention computation is a bottleneck in your self-hosted service.
builder_plan.change: Check the supported GPU, tensor shapes, and precision, then replace only the relevant kernel.
builder_plan.baseline: The existing kernel inside the same complete serving pipeline.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Numerical differences, end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory at realistic shapes.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI Inference
summary: TKCC replaces manually tuned kernels and fixed engine configurations with a persistent agent loop that continually compiles and hill-climbs the inference forward pass, using a tiered persistent engine for high-fidelity measurement and a cost model to seed parallelism choices. The cost is substantial engineering complexity: a custom persistent engine layer, agent context management, and continuous compilation infrastructure, plus dependence on proprietary tooling not publicly available. It can fail when workload distributions shift faster than the agent loop converges, when low-fidelity kernel benchmarks mislead optimization for data-dependent operations like MoE routing, or when compiled artifacts overfit to measured traffic and regress under real serving conditions.
rationale: The reported gains are real but come from a proprietary production system requiring fleet-scale infrastructure and continual agent orchestration that a single-GPU, budget-constrained team cannot replicate, so it should be monitored rather than adopted.
technique: Agent-driven continual compilation for inference engines

claims.statement: TKCC replaces manually tuned kernels and fixed engine configurations with a persistent agent loop that continually compiles and hill-climbs the inference forward pass, using a tiered persistent engine for high-fidelity measurement and a cost model to seed parallelism choices. The cost is substantial engineering complexity: a custom persistent engine layer, agent context management, and continuous compilation infrastructure, plus dependence on proprietary tooling not publicly available. It can fail when workload distributions shift faster than the agent loop converges, when low-fidelity kernel benchmarks mislead optimization for data-dependent operations like MoE routing, or when compiled artifacts overfit to measured traffic and regress under real serving conditions.

Up to 2.6x higher TPS than the best open-source engines on frontier models on the InferenceX benchmark, and up to 1.7x over hand-written Megakernels on a Llama 1B workload; batch-size-1 records of 1111-1205 TPS on specific models.
